To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the carbohydrate-binding module from the bacterial sialidases from Micromonspora viridifaciensi binds to the galactoside moiety of lactose and galactose, and that the galactose-binding site sits above the active site of the catalytic domain.

The CBM of the M. viiridifaciens Sialidase recognizes galactose and that the flexibility of the CBM and the immunoglobulin domain may facilitate the binding of galactose residues to the sialidase catalytic site.

the galactose-binding domain of the sialidase of M. viridificens has a flexible linker between the galactose and sialic acid binding sites, that the galactoside-binding site of the sialic acid-binding domain is a cleft, and that the galactopyranose-binding site has a hydrophobic patch that binds to the pyranose ring.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular basis of the interaction between the CBM and its ligand.
the structure of the CBM of the M. Viridifaciens Sialidase and
the structure and function of enzymes involved in the degradation of complex carbohydrates and their role in human health.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
galactose recognition by this CBM occurs via a combination of hydrogen bonding, hydrophobic interactions and van der Waals contacts.

the CBM is involved in the targeting of the enzyme towards glycoconjugate substrates, and that the galactose-binding site is located above the active site, which may be involved in the binding of the substrate.

galactose binding by the M. viidifaciens carbohydrate-binding module is not a prerequisite for sialidase activity, but rather that the galactose-binding site may be involved in the targeting of the enzyme to specific substrates.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have determined nine structures of MvSia and have analysed the relative flexibility of each of the three domains.
the M. virifaciens sialiase has an inter-domain flexibility, which may play an important role in its catalysis.
we have studied the flexibility of a three domain enzyme and shown that the CBM is flexible and can bind a variety of galactosides.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the galactose recognition site is not a simple binding pocket but is a complex surface that is capable of binding a wide variety of ligands.
the galactose-binding site is located in the CBM and is in close proximity to the catalytic site.
the CBM of the M. viridifaciens  sialidase recognizes galactose and galactose-containing oligosaccharides, and that this recognition is likely to be important for the enzyme's function in nature.
